answer_text: Copper slowly reacts with air, carbon dioxide and moisture to form a green coating of basic copper carbonate. That layer sticks to the metal and prevents further corrosion, so a copper dome lasts. Iron would form rust, Fe2O3.xH2O, which is loose and flakes off, exposing fresh iron until the structure weakens. Copper is also highly malleable, so it can be beaten into thin sheets and curved to the shape of a roof.
